title: Canary decision heuristics and escalation grid (working)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures a compact, decision-focused set of heuristics for running canaries and A/B experiments for inference-facing features (model swaps, quantization changes, cache behavior, routing policy changes). The goal: give engineers, product, SRE and CS quick, operational rules to decide: continue, pause, rollback, or escalate to incident.
body_cont:
Why a separate heuristics + escalation grid?
- Many rollout docs describe ceremony and observability. Teams still struggle with ‘what do I do at 95th percentile?’ in the middle of a spike.
- This file is intentionally procedural: short rules, threshold examples, who to call, and what minimal mitigation to trigger.

Definitions (quick):
- Canary: small percentage of traffic routed to a new model/variant/policy.
- Experiment (A/B): persistent split with analysis window; typically longer and more tolerant to noise.
- Safety fallback: automatic route that directs to prior baseline model or to a lightweight fallback mode (e.g., static response or degraded reasoning mode).

Primary risk buckets we gate on:
1) Latency regressions (p95, p99, TTFI)
2) Output quality regressions (eval-based metrics, production quality checks, customer-reported NPS)
3) Error rate regressions (5xx, streaming disconnects, decoder failures)
4) Cost anomalies (token cost or infra cost per request)
5) Safety regressions (toxicity, hallucinations on seed prompt sets)
6) Availability and cascading impacts (queue growth, KV cache pressure)

Decision heuristics (short form):
- If p95 latency increases > 30% relative to baseline AND p99 > 20% increase -> pause canary and notify SRE/product.
- If client-visible error rate (4xx/5xx user-facing) increases by absolute > 0.5% over baseline for more than 10 minutes -> immediate rollback.
- If safety metric (toxicity score, hallucination detections) regresses by > 10% on validated prompt set -> pause and escalate to Safety/Applied ML.
- If cost per 1k tokens increases > 40% and not offset by quality gains (manual spot-check required) -> throttle exposure and set meeting for tradeoff decision.
- If small signal spikes < 5 minutes and isolated to a single region or host -> monitor 15 minutes before action (unless error rate high).

Escalation grid (who to call, sequence):
- Triage (first 10 minutes): owner on-call (engineer who deployed), runbook owner (Product rollout PM), on-call SRE. Post message to #canary-ops with short summary and preliminary metrics.
- Tactical (10–30 minutes): if autoscaling or fallback didn't materialize -> SRE lead + serving runtime engineer + PM. Consider immediate traffic cut to baseline or route to dedicated capacity.
- Incident (30+ minutes OR severe user impact): PagerDuty page to SRE incident leader, Eng manager of serving runtime, Head of Product. Post incident channel and start incident doc.

Runbook actions by decision outcome (concise):
- Pause: stop traffic increases, freeze rollout configuration, keep canary at current exposure (e.g., hold 5%). Observe 30 minutes, collect logs, annotate anomalies.
- Rollback: redirect canary traffic back to baseline model variant, confirm stabilization across p50/p95/p99 and error rates, run regression eval against canary-held prompts.
- Throttle: decrease exposure (e.g., 5% -> 1% -> 0.1%) progressively while running diagnostics. Use automated scripted route-change to avoid manual error.
- Hotfix escalate: if the regression is traced to a runtime kernel or quantization regressor, patch and deploy to canary only after sign-off from applied-ml and runtime owner.

Checklist before unpausing/retrying a canary:
- Root cause notes attached to canary experiment ticket.
- Repro script (small harness) that reproduces the regression locally or in staging.
- Regression test set run: 1000 prompts with baseline vs canary diff and human spot-check of samples showing top-10 failures.
- Observability: dashboards updated (latency, errors, cost, safety), tracing enabled for representative requests, KV cache hit rates captured.
- Postmortem stub created if we paused/rolled back.

Examples (short scenarios):
1) Model swap (v2 quantized): p95 +45%, p99 +60%, cost +10%, safety unchanged.
Action: pause -> rollback recommended since latency regressed >30%. Create ticket for kernel optimization; re-run quantization profile in test harness.

2) Routing policy change (add region-tier fallback): error spike in EU region only for 12 minutes, p99 normal globally.
Action: Pause new routing in EU (regional slice) and throttle to 0.5% EU only; SRE to investigate region-specific infra. No global rollback.

3) A/B (re-ranking model test) shows small quality uptick but cost +70% and endpoints' GPU utilization steady.
Action: Throttle exposure, tag experiment for biz/eng cost review, escalate to PM for go/no-go within 48h. If revenue/engagement not aligned, rollback.

Instrument checklist (minimum metrics we must have for a canary):
- p50/p95/p99 latency per route and per region
- request success rate (2xx) and client-visible 4xx/5xx rate
- token usage per request and cost-per-request estimate
- safety signal rate (automated classifier score) and curated prompt hits
- trace sampling (1% baseline + 100% for error traces)
- autoscaler signals and queue depth

Roles & responsibilities (practical):
- Deploy owner (on-call engineer or author of change): initiate pause/rollback via router CLI, annotate experiment ticket with immediate findings.
- Product PM (rollout): validates user-visible impact and customer comms, coordinates postmortem and prioritization.
- Applied ML lead: triage quality regressions, validate eval cluster runs, recommend model fixes.
- Serving runtime owner: triage kernel/runtime/quantization regressions, coordinate hotfix path.
- SRE on-call: manage capacity, autoscaling and routing changes, lead incident if availability impacted.
- Customer success (if affected customers): prepare templated comms, collect customer-reported failures.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (notes):
- Absolute thresholds vs relative baselining: prefer rolling windows and seasonality adjustments — we need a small library to compute relative delta adjusting for diurnal patterns.
- How much automation? Automatic rollback on severe errors vs requiring human approval — propose: critical error rate thresholds trigger automated rollback, all other thresholds stay manual. (need PD policy change).
- Region vs global thresholds: should thresholds be normalized per-region by historical noise. (we currently do not).

Quick templates (Slack snippets / comms):
- Pause notice (ops): "Canary paused for X at 12:10 UTC. p95 +44% vs baseline. Owner: @aisha. Triage channel: #canary-ops. Next update in 15m."
- Rollback notice (ops): "Canary rolled back to baseline at 12:30 UTC following sustained error rate increase. Incident doc: <doc link>."

Action items (next steps):
- Build a small relative-delta helper (python) for product dashboards — assigned Diego, due 2025-02-10.
- Add region-normalized thresholds to telemetry — SRE backlog INF-8932.
- Author automated rollback policy proposal and PD runbook — Marco to draft by 2025-02-07.
- Run a tabletop with SRE/Product/Applied ML on a simulated P99 outage in March — Claire to schedule.

Notes to self (working fragments):
- Keep examples short; ops need one-pagers, not essays.
- Tie safety checks to the exact prompt-corpus used in the last training/validation to reduce false positives.
- Consider a lightweight canary mode that samples 10% of tokens through the new model but still returns baseline output unless checks pass (for instrumentation-heavy experiments).

References and heuristics sources:
- Our internal rollout playbooks (link above), SRE latency SLO playbook, Applied ML evaluation guidelines.
- External: Netflix/Spinnaker post-deploy rollback heuristics (inspired), Google SRE runbook patterns.

If you're reading this as an on-call: use the Slack snippets above, confirm who owns the canary ticket, and default to rollback if unsure when user-visible errors are rising. We can iterate thresholds after 3–5 experiment runs.
